statement: Whether Egyptian hieroglyphs or Mesopotamian proto-cuneiform is earlier is genuinely unresolved, contrary to older popular sources that default to cuneiform priority. Tomb U-j at Abydos (excavated by Günter Dreyer, discovered 1988), containing ~150+ inscribed bone/ivory labels, dates to c. 3320-3150 BCE — overlapping substantially with proto-cuneiform Uruk IV (c. 3350-3200 BCE per CDLI) within each side's own dating uncertainty. The two systems emerged within the same roughly 200-year window in the late 4th millennium BCE; priority cannot currently be established with confidence.
scholarly_disagreement: The comparative-earliness question between Egypt and Mesopotamia is live and unresolved; treat as UNCERTAIN, not resolvable to a single answer from current evidence.

sources.citation: Dreyer, Günter. Excavations at Abydos, Tomb U-j, 1988 and subsequent seasons (German Archaeological Institute, Cairo).
sources.author: Günter Dreyer

sources.citation: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative (CDLI), periods reference.

does_not_demonstrate: That cuneiform was definitively first (a common older popular-source framing not supported by the current dating overlap)
